verses.text: At this my heart trembles and feels like it might leap out of my chest.
Listen closely to the rumble of God’s voice, the sound that comes from his mouth.
He sends it across the whole sky and sends his lightning to the ends of the earth.
Then comes the roar. He thunders with a majestic voice and holds nothing back when it is heard.
God’s voice thunders in ways that fill us with wonder. He does great things we can’t understand.
He tells the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and gives the same command to the rain, even to the heaviest downpour.
He brings everyone’s work to a stop so the people he made can see what he’s doing.
The animals take shelter and stay in their dens.
The storm comes out of its chamber, and the cold comes from the north.
God breathes out and ice forms. Even broad stretches of water freeze over.
He loads the thick clouds with moisture and spreads out the clouds that flash with his lightning.
He steers them wherever he wants, so they do what he commands across the inhabited world.
He sends them to correct people, to care for his land, or to show his faithful love.
Listen to this, Job. Stand still and think about the wonders God does.
Do you know how God directs the clouds and makes lightning flash from them?
Do you know how the clouds work? These are the wonders of the one whose knowledge is complete.
Do you know why your clothes feel so warm when the south wind leaves the land still?
Can you help him spread out the sky, as hard as a mirror cast from metal?
Tell us what we should say to him. We’re in the dark and can’t put our case together.
Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?
People can’t see the bright light in the sky until the wind blows through and clears it.
Golden splendor comes out of the north. God is clothed in awe-inspiring majesty.
We can’t reach the Almighty. His power is beyond us, and with all his justice and righteousness he never oppresses anyone.
That’s why people revere him. He pays no special attention to those who think themselves wise.
